solution:
Let the correspondence send A to X, B to Y and C to Z.

AB corresponds to QR, so \(\{X, Y\} = \{Q, R\}\); BC corresponds to PR, so \(\{Y, Z\} = \{P, R\}\); CA corresponds to PQ, so \(\{Z, X\} = \{P, Q\}\).

Intersecting these gives X = Q, Y = R, Z = P, i.e. \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle QRP\), which is the same statement as \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle CAB\).

Checking option B directly: \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle CAB\) gives \(\frac{PQ}{CA} = \frac{QR}{AB} = \frac{PR}{CB}\), i.e. \(\frac{AB}{QR} = \frac{BC}{PR} = \frac{CA}{PQ}\) — exactly the given proportion.

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is (B).

solution:
\(\angle D \cong \angle Q\) and \(\angle E \cong \angle R\), so the remaining angles also correspond: \(\angle F \cong \angle P\).

\(\therefore \triangle DEF \sim \triangle QRP\), and the corresponding sides are DE and QR, EF and RP, DF and QP.

\(\therefore \frac{DE}{QR} = \frac{EF}{RP} = \frac{DF}{QP}\)

Option A \(\left(\frac{EF}{PR} = \frac{DF}{PQ}\right)\), option C \(\left(\frac{DE}{QR} = \frac{DF}{PQ}\right)\) and option D \(\left(\frac{EF}{RP} = \frac{DE}{QR}\right)\) are all restatements of this and are true.

Option B pairs DE with PQ, but DE corresponds to QR, not to PQ. So option B is the false statement.

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is (B).

solution:
\(\angle B = \angle E\) and \(\angle C = \angle F\), so two angles of one triangle are congruent to two corresponding angles of the other.

\(\therefore \triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\) .......... AA test of similarity

AB = 3DE, so \(\frac{AB}{DE} = 3 \neq 1\). Congruent triangles would need every ratio of corresponding sides to be 1.

\(\therefore\) the triangles are similar but not congruent, which is option (B).

solution:
All equilateral triangles are similar, so the theorem of areas of similar triangles applies.

\(\frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle DEF)} = \frac{AB^2}{DE^2}\)

\(\therefore \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4^2}{DE^2}\)

\(\therefore DE^2 = 32\) \(\therefore DE = \sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}\)

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is (D).

solution:
seg XY \(\parallel\) seg BC with X on AB and Y on AC, so \(\triangle AXY \sim \triangle ABC\) by the AA test.

\(\therefore \frac{AX}{AB} = \frac{AY}{AC}\)

Cross-multiplying, \(AX \times AC = AY \times AB\), i.e. \(\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{AX}{AY}\), which is option (A).

The others fail on a concrete case: take AB = 10, AC = 8, AX = 5; then XB = 5, AY = 4, YC = 4.

Option B: \(\frac{AX}{XB} = 1\) but \(\frac{AY}{AC} = 0.5\).

Option C: \(\frac{AX}{YC} = 1.25\) but \(\frac{AY}{XB} = 0.8\).

Option D: \(\frac{AB}{YC} = 2.5\) but \(\frac{AC}{XB} = 1.6\).

\(\therefore\) the correct alternative is (A).
